steps.name: Logos
steps.text: What are you looking at?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: At your King of Sarkaz, Banshee.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: You're facing Amiya.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I advise you to carefully consider your actions.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: And you should do away with the curses in your hands.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Relax. They've already won.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I'm grateful for our earlier exchanges, Damazti. I have a clearer understanding of your methods now.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: The King of Sarkaz couldn't have possibly lost to our clone that had already been fried near to a crisp by a Draco's flames.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: But we are glad to have experienced something new for the first time in such a long time.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: It's been ages since we've seen anything that has brought us even a speck of excitement.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Be proud of yourself, Banshee. You've convinced us, and we'll be more than happy to keep this new possibility of yours, though we're still not very optimistic about the direction this possibility is heading.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: But to us, time and patience are two things we have more than plenty of.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We will meet again, at the next finish line.

spans.text: meet again, at the next finish line.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Where are you going next?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We've never gone anywhere on purpose, we merely wander the land.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: You've mentioned before, Damazti, that you've pretty much exhausted all possibilities.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: But there remains uncharted territory for you.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Everything on this great land is constantly evolving, while you stayed just as you always have been, imitating the fruits of evolution.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Yes, you've never gone anywhere, and yet you're already complete.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: So of course there can be no progress in something that's already been completed.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: How persuasively provocative. And what do you suggest?

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: You've already guessed it.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Heralding our deaths—you do live up to your name, bean sí.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: From death comes new life.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Indeed, we've never tried this before...

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We just bid goodbye to a friend, at a place not far from here.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: She said that she would rather give up living than to let life wash over her.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We felt her emotions, we saw her determination.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: She claimed it was the choice of a coward, but we felt something else.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We could barely put it in words then, but now we know, that it also took a certain kind of courage.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: The kind of courage we've never considered before.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Well, alright. Banshee, we admit it

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We've begun looking forward to this.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: This might be just an innocuous scheme of yours, a clumsy method of ridding yourself of an enemy.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: But that doesn't matter to us.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Or maybe the souls are merely borrowing your voice to provoke us.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Need me to help you?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: How about you leave us with some decency?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Though you ought to sound the death knell for us.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: You sure are a tenacious and brave bunch. Celebrate your victory.

options: This can't be your full power.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: What, are you not entertained, Doctor of Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Or maybe that's unnecessary? Maybe we actually understand you on a... level beyond your worst estimates?

options: I trust Rhodes Island's security systems.
Do you also have a clone on Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Haha, relax, Doctor. Your ship's onboarding inspection is not as easy as it seems to slip through.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Alright. Goodbye, all.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: What are you planning?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: What else can we do with our broken body?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We've stayed in our original form for... long enough.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Tiny King of Sarkaz, where will you go next?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Where will you bring these people who trust you, follow you, protect you?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Will you do as Buldrokkas'tee prophesized, and enslave everything across all the lands...?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Or will you prove that it is only us who have been bound too deeply by the chains of history?

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: 'Evolution,' a tricky word indeed, implying an inevitable progress, though it may not be.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: But no matter, you will find your path, and us as well.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: He dissipated...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: No, the Damazti won't die. His other, more complete and stronger self, is probably just around the corner.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: This is a typical tactic of his, to have the prey let down its guard, and then come in for the kill...

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: A bone whistle? How can this be?

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: Logos sees the bone whistle as a lamentable tradition of the Royal Court, and has always refused to sound it as his predecessors have done.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: But this is indeed a bone whistle from the Master of Knells.

steps.name: Ascalon
steps.text: The Damazti cluster... is dying.

a.text: 'The elegy has sounded, the bone whistle done wailing.'
'I serve as a witness to a Sarkaz, the Damazti, and his cluster.'

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: A bone whistle.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: How long has it been since we've had the Lord of the Banshees grace our court to sound the bone whistle?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Damazti Cluster has died.

steps.name: Confessarius
steps.text: Fret not, the Damazti has only encountered a minor setback, he'll soon...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: No, what I mean is, every Damazti fragment is simultaneously decaying.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Damazti dies, and our long-lasting Royal Court will collapse.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Hmph, how interesting.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I think, that he himself never imagined that it would end like this.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: How should I describe it? A split into halves?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Or the birth of two new lives?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The ancient Damazti no longer exists.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And two newborn Damazti have appeared in this world.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Sand in nature is regarded as the final state of all things. No matter how strong a boulder may be, it turns to dust at the end of time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But then again, the sand may also hold the possibility of starting a cycle of reincarnation anew.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Kal'tsit, your wounds are still healing, move another inch and I'll tell Shining—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'm already fine, for the most part.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: An old friend might locate us soon... no, I should say a new friend now.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I don't want to meet any of your old or new friends.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: There's good news and bad news, pick one?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wait, I sure am tired. Why did I think you would be up for a stupid game?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The bad news is—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Give me the good news.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The bad news is that we didn't find the entrance to the Sarkaz supply route in Brentwood. There was no underground tunnel at all, but there was a passage used for inspections...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Wait, you... huh?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I said, give me the good news.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ah... um, I...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Shining—!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I like to hear positive news sometimes as well, Closure.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: The good news is, we managed to get in touch with the Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Thank you for your assistance, Duke Windermere. We've managed to re-establish our communication channels.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The refugees we brought have all boarded the ship, and they'll be under the Duke of Windermere's protection for the time being.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I should be the one thanking you, Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: You've helped the townspeople of Norport Borough escape a disaster. Not all of them, but... it's enough.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Protecting the people is what we, those who bear the title of duke, ought to do.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: And, you even saved my daughter.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: She was just bawling in her room earlier.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Mum! I was only...

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I can guess what you've all been through the last couple of days.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: But Delphine, perhaps you have come to better understand how those in power should wield authority.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: If I may be so bold, Your Grace, how are you planning to use your power?

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: After witnessing the fate of the Steam Knights, I'm not sure—

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I had to make a strategic decision, daughter of Montague.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: You may call it a plot, and I won't deny that I signed my name on the Steam Knights' orders.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: But... to decide the future of this country is exactly our duty.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...'Duty'.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Yes, Miss Vina. 'Duty'.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: You understand why I'm addressing you that way.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If you'd excuse us, Your Grace. For now, I would... rather be with my friends.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: As you please.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Now then, Doctor of Rhodes Island. I believe... we can't avoid discussing the object your operator is carrying.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: I knew it wasn't my imagination.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: That is Victoria's Realmblade, yes?

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Delphine was praising you so highly that perhaps I require a re-evaluation.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Anyway, it's impossible to ignore her and the sword she's carrying.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Delphine told me about your deal with her. Even though there were some twists and turns in between, I'm sure that deal remains valid.

options: Don't tell me you're becoming a supporter of Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: But I promise you that for now, I'll act as if nothing happened.

steps.name: Duke of Windermere
steps.text: We can talk this out slowly when we've returned to my demesne.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Cador didn't get on the ship, he left with a bunch of people.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: And Hannah?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: She's still in her room and refuses to come out.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Let's get her something to eat. She's barely had a decent meal in Norport.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: What are you burning?

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: A bunch of drafts.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Notes I saved for writing inspiration.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: But I forgot where I dropped my memoir notebook, haha.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Siege, you don't need it, do you? We don't need it anymore.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Dagda
steps.text: Siege, what's... are you crying?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No, I just...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I just...
Heavy tears roll down Siege's cheeks, while Morgan and Dagda are both stunned in their common consensus—Vina has never shed a tear before.
On the deck of this high-speed battleship, the Victorian sun is still slowly rising, sweeping the haze and evaporating the mist from last night.
And this youth called Vina, with her back to the sun, is expressing her emotions without a word.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: I just... got ash in my eyes.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Norport will return to her old self, the people are still there after all.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: We'll get our old lives back... eventually.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: We just... need patience. A little more of it.

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: Vina, I—

steps.name: Morgan
steps.text: The war is going to end, right?
